Step 1: Analyze Assertion (A): Real crystals of $\text{CO}$, $\text{NO}$, $\text{N}_2\text{O}$, and ice ($	ext{H}_2	ext{O}$) have measurable non-zero entropy at $0\text{ K}$ (residual entropy $\approx R \ln 2 \approx 5.8\text{ J K}^{-1}\text{ mol}^{-1}$ for $\text{CO}$). Thus, (A) is true.
Step 2: Analyze Reason (R): Because the dipole moment of $\text{CO}$ is very small ($0.11\text{ D}$), the energy difference between orientations $\cdots \text{C}-\text{O}\cdots\text{C}-\text{O}\cdots$ and $\cdots \text{C}-\text{O}\cdots\text{O}-\text{C}\cdots$ is extremely small. As temperature drops, the molecules lack sufficient thermal energy to reorient into a perfectly ordered arrangement, locking in random orientations ($W > 1$). Thus, (R) is true.
Step 3: Evaluate connection: The orientational randomness described in Reason (R) is the exact physical origin of residual entropy at $0\text{ K}$. Therefore, (R) is the correct explanation of (A).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText:
Consider the following chemical and physical processes:
(I) Dissolution of crystalline table sugar (sucrose) in water
(II) Rusting of metallic iron: $4\text{Fe}(s) + 3\text{O}_2(g) \longrightarrow 2\text{Fe}_2\text{O}_3(s)$
(III) Thermal decomposition: $\text{CaCO}_3(s) \longrightarrow \text{CaO}(s) + \text{CO}_2(g)$
(IV) Condensation of water vapor: $\text{H}_2\text{O}(g) \longrightarrow \text{H}_2\text{O}(l)$
(V) Denaturation of globular egg albumin protein upon boiling
(VI) Polymerization of ethene: $n\text{CH}_2=\text{CH}_2(g) \longrightarrow -(\text{CH}_2-\text{CH}_2)_n-(s)$
Which of the following combinations represents ALL the processes in which entropy increases ($\Delta S > 0$)?
options: A) (II), (IV), and (VI)
B) (I), (III), and (V)
C) (I), (II), and (III)
D) (III), (IV), and (VI)
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Evaluate entropy changes for each process:
- (I) Sugar dissolving in water: Solid ordered crystal breaks into dispersed hydrated molecules, increasing disorder $\implies \Delta S > 0$.
- (II) Rusting of iron: $3\text{ moles of gas}$ are consumed to form a solid, leading to substantial loss of randomness $\implies \Delta S < 0$.
- (III) Decomposition of $\text{CaCO}_3$: Gaseous $\text{CO}_2$ is liberated from solid, increasing gaseous moles $\implies \Delta S > 0$.
- (IV) Condensation of steam: Gas transitions to ordered liquid $\implies \Delta S < 0$.
- (V) Denaturation of protein: Ordered globular tertiary/secondary structure unfolds into randomized coiled chains $\implies \Delta S > 0$.
- (VI) Polymerization: Many free gaseous monomer molecules become constrained in a single polymer chain $\implies \Delta S < 0$.
Step 2: Collect all processes with $\Delta S > 0$: (I), (III), and (V).
Step 3: Conclusion: The combination showing an increase in entropy is (I), (III), and (V).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText:
For the standard electrochemical Daniell cell reaction:
$$\text{Zn}(s) + \text{Cu}^{2+}(aq) \rightleftharpoons \text{Zn}^{2+}(aq) + \text{Cu}(s)$$
the standard cell potential at $298\text{ K}$ is $E_{\text{cell}}^\circ = +1.10\text{ V}$. Given Faraday's constant $F = 96500\text{ C mol}^{-1}$, what is the standard Gibbs free energy change ($\Delta_r G^\circ$) for this cell reaction at $298\text{ K}$?

Step 1: Identify the number of electrons transferred ($n$):
$$\text{Zn}(s) \longrightarrow \text{Zn}^{2+}(aq) + 2e^-\quad (\text{oxidation half-reaction})$$
$$\text{Cu}^{2+}(aq) + 2e^- \longrightarrow \text{Cu}(s)\quad (\text{reduction half-reaction})$$
Here, $n = 2\text{ moles of electrons}$.
Step 2: Use the thermodynamic relationship between $\Delta_r G^\circ$ and $E_{\text{cell}}^\circ$:
$$\Delta_r G^\circ = -n F E_{\text{cell}}^\circ$$
Step 3: Calculate $\Delta_r G^\circ$:
$$\Delta_r G^\circ = -2 \times 96500\text{ C mol}^{-1} \times 1.10\text{ V}$$
Since $1\text{ J} = 1\text{ C} \cdot \text{V}$:
$$\Delta_r G^\circ = -212300\text{ J mol}^{-1} = -212.3\text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$$
Step 4: Conclusion: The standard Gibbs free energy change is $-212.3\text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$.
